subject: Pen test workpapers, methodology, and report age — acceptance for SOC 2 evidence
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-security@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pen test evidence acceptance question (report dated 2025-09)

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question from our audit team: we received Redwood's pen test summary dated 2025-09-30 during the SOC 2 evidence pull. The auditor is flagging the report age — their baseline is 12 months but they will consider older reports with additional artifacts.

Could Redwood provide: 1) a short note on the pen test methodology and standards the firm used (e.g., OWASP, NIST SP800-115, manual verification scope), 2) workpapers or test traces that show remediation verification, and 3) a signed attestation from the vendor indicating no material system changes since the engagement?

If you can share a redacted set of workpapers and an attestation letter, that should help our SOC reviewer accept the evidence. Is there any limitation on redacting IP or customer data?

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Security Analyst, Acme Corp

--
Alice Monroe
Acme Corp | security@acme.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-15T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence acceptance question (report dated 2025-09)

Hi Alice — thanks for the note and the level of detail. Im looping in Karthik and Mina from our security team to provide the technical artifacts and an attestation workflow.

High level: Redwood engages independent firms for annual penetration testing and we also perform targeted internal follow-ups when significant infra or code changes occur. We can provide: a redacted set of workpapers, a signed attestation letter from the vendor, and a short methodology summary. Ill let Karthik/Mina propose what we can share safely and how we suggest redaction.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence acceptance question (report dated 2025-09)

Hi Alice — Karthik here from Redwood Security.

Thanks for outlining the auditors requirement. To be explicit on methodology: the engagement was conducted by an external vendor (TrustedSec Solutions) following a blended approach — automated scanning, OWASP Top 10-focused manual verification, and targeted infrastructure tests mapped to NIST SP 800-115 techniques. The scope included all public-facing inference endpoints, the private API used by our console, and the administrative portal.

What we can provide now (attached/linked):
- A redacted workpapers bundle (test cases + evidence screenshots / request/response traces) that omits customer data and internal IPs. Filename: redwood_pt_workpapers.zip
- A signed attestation letter from the vendor confirming there were no material findings outstanding and no material changes to scope components since the engagement date: redwood_attestation_letter_signed.pdf
- The pen test summary (executive findings): pt_summary_2026-09.pdf (note: the summary you have is 2025-09; we issued an updated executive summary in 2026-09 after a targeted re-test of priority findings)

About report age acceptance: our standard posture is annual testing. In practice auditors will accept a report older than 12 months up to ~15 months if: 1) there is a vendor attestation of no material changes, 2) redacted workpapers are provided showing remediation verification, and 3) there have been no major infra or architecture changes. If Acmes SOC reviewer needs stricter limits (12 months), we can discuss an ad-hoc scoped assessment / retest.

On redactions: we will redact customer payloads, specific customer identifiers, internal IPs, and any raw logs that contain PII. We will preserve request/response patterns, reproduction steps, and screenshots that demonstrate remediation.

Ive uploaded the workpapers to a secure drive and attached the attestation and the 2026 summary for your auditor review. If the auditor needs signed chain-of-custody or more granular traces, we can evaluate providing limited encrypted artifacts under an NDA.

Cc also: Mina for remediation verification notes.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence acceptance question (report dated 2025-09)

Hi Alice,

Following up with remediation details and timing: the September 2025 engagement found three medium issues and one high issue. All four had tracked remediation owners and we completed internal verification steps as follows:

- High issue (auth bypass)  corrective code fix deployed 2025-11-12; verification performed by vendor re-test (2026-03) and internal smoke tests on 2026-03-05. Evidence: reproduction steps and post-fix response traces (included in workpapers).
- Mediums  remediated between 2025-10 and 2026-01 with CWE references and ticket links. We include the internal ticket IDs and summary notes (redacted).

Policy on report validity: Redwood supports our customers' auditors by providing attested workpapers and an attestation letter; auditors typically accept past reports up to 15 months with those artifacts. If your auditor requires a <12-month report we recommend scheduling a scoped retest — we can do a focused re-test (3-5 days) against the same components for $X,XXX and provide results within 10 business days.

Attached: redwood_attestation_letter_signed.pdf, redwood_pt_workpapers.zip, pt_summary_2026-09.pdf

If youd like, we can do a 30-minute call with our vendor (TrustedSec) and our remediation lead to walk the auditor through the workpapers. Let me know availability.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

--
Attachment stubs: redwood_pt_workpapers.zip (10MB archived workpapers, redacted); redwood_attestation_letter_signed.pdf (signed by TrustedSec lead); pt_summary_2026-09.pdf (2 pages)

Also, Alice Romero from our audit team would like a 30-minute walkthrough with TrustedSec and your remediation lead next week (Nov 22 or 23). Can you confirm availability?

Appreciate the quick coordination.
